R4:interp.title: Latent-knowledge probes for statement fidelity
R4:interp.summary: Probes on a formalizer or auditor that predict 'misformalized' when the model internally knows its Lean differs from the English (ELK-style; Mallen et al. recover 89% of the AUROC gap). This is the only option aimed at the core bottleneck. It fails when every model shares the misreading, and LLM errors are correlated. It can be trained on the Formal Conjectures and PutnamBench fix pairs. Untested; §7 proposes the experiment.

R4:interp.title: Cross-representation comparison of English and Lean
R4:interp.summary: Compare middle-layer representations of the informal and formal statements, building on the semantic hub result that code and arithmetic share a space with language. It would be a meaning-level check that does not depend on what the auditor writes, but nothing shows it can separate fine distinctions such as natural vs lower density, and SAE features capture concepts only in fragments. Most speculative option.

roots.question: Can scientific paper reviews (maybe specifically ML, DL, data-driven papers) be automated with highly scoped, small subagents following the AISLE model: many open-source models, since they have different blind spots, with tasks scoped to known failure modes like biases, factual reproduction errors, 'do these authors/papers exist' errors and overclaims, including building the suggested experiments and variations and running them on GPUs? Is compute a major blocker at some level, could a shit ton of GPU parallelism fix it?

What's actually stopping general purpose robot hands from reliably doing stuff like folding laundry or loading a dishwasher? Is it the lack of real-world manipulation data, the hardware (sensors, actuators, tactile feedback), or the sim-to-real gap? Is that a major blocker at some level, and could it be fixed by running millions of simulated robots in parallel on a shit ton of GPUs?

Why can't we predict earthquakes days or hours in advance? Is it fundamentally chaotic physics that no model can get around, or is it mostly a data problem with too few sensors and too few big quakes to learn from? Could training huge foundation models on decades of global seismic waveforms, GPS strain and fault simulations with a shit ton of GPU parallelism actually get somewhere, or is compute not the blocker at all?

What actually stops us from autoformalizing most of published math into Lean? Is it gaps in Mathlib coverage, the step of translating informal proofs where authors skip things that are 'obvious', or something deeper about how mathematicians write? The Lean kernel is a free and perfect verifier, so this looks like one of the few domains where brute-force search can't fool itself. Could you split every paper into tiny lemma-sized subgoals and throw many different open-source prover models at each one in parallel, with each model scoped to a known failure mode like wrong definitions, mismatched conventions or silently strengthened hypotheses? Is compute a major blocker at some level, and could a shit ton of GPU parallelism fix it, or is the real bottleneck checking that the formal statement means the same thing as the English one?

What limits general-purpose robot manipulation right now? Is it lack of real-world data, the sim-to-real gap, or hardware like hands and tactile sensors? If you can already run millions of simulated environments in parallel on GPUs with heavy domain randomization, why can't you brute-force a policy that folds laundry or ties knots and then transfers to a real robot? Is contact and deformable-object physics the wall that no amount of compute gets you over because the simulator itself is wrong in ways you can't randomize away? Or could a shit ton of GPU parallelism plus a small fleet of real robots that keeps correcting the simulator close the loop?

plan.option_title: O3: does the model know its Lean differs from the English?
plan.question: Can a linear probe on a model's activations detect misformalized Lean statements better than the model's own Yes/No answer, a Lean-only probe, or a strong LLM judge?
plan.hypothesis: A probe on a 32B model's activations separates wrong from fixed Lean better than the model's own verdict, because models may know more than they say [mallen].

held_fixed: Same Formal Conjectures train/test split grouped by PR and problem file

Pre-fixed decision thresholds (set before looking at test data)
Temporal test sets starting after each model's release

predictions.if_lever: Probe AUROC reaches at least 0.75 on fixes made after model release, beats the model's own verdict by 0.05, and catches 25% of the strong judge's misses.
predictions.if_not: Probe gains vanish when the informal statement is removed (gap at most 0.03), or probe and judge miss the same items, as the skeptic's concern says.
predictions.decision_rule: O3 is a real second channel if transfer-probe AUROC >= 0.75 on post-cutoff fixes, Delta-control >= 0.10, probe beats B1 by >= 0.05, and it catches >= 25% of B4's misses with McNemar p < 0.05. O3 reads style, not fidelity, if Delta-control <= 0.03 or B0 ~ probe.
predictions.noise_rule: Bootstrap CIs resampling PRs; Hanley-McNeil half-width about +/-0.04 at 300 pairs; probe fitting rerun with three seeds and fold assignments; judges sampled k=4; margins of 0.05-0.10 set above the CI half-width.
predictions.expected_why: The file states no expected outcome; it says only that GPUs are not the binding input and that labels and Lean-literate review are.

plan.compute_tested_why: The plan tests whether a probe beats other detectors, not how results change with more compute. The file says GPUs are not the binding input (NOT-COMPUTE-BOUND verdict).
plan.scored_against: Human-fixed labels: Formal Conjectures merged misformalization PRs (wrong Lean before, fixed Lean after), plus CriticLeanBench labels and a few PutnamBench fixes.

novelty.closest_prior: Mallen et al. found probes usually report a model's knowledge independently of its output; Goodfire used difference-of-means from synthetic code to detect real reward hacking [mallen]. Neither tested Lean statement fidelity.
novelty.left_open: Whether probes detect real Lean misformalizations beyond what the model says and beyond a strong LLM judge, tested on real merged fixes.

limits: Fixed statements may differ from wrong ones in style, not fidelity. One author wrote 268 of 515 PRs and 239 were merged in one month. A fixed statement may still be wrong, inflating false-positive rates.

pick.title: Cross-representation comparison of English and Lean

plan.option_title: O4 Cross-representation comparison of the English and Lean statements
plan.question: Do a model's hidden states for an English statement and its Lean formalization drift apart when the formalization is wrong, and is that more useful than a text judge or cheap baselines?
plan.hypothesis: Expected to fail on fine-grained errors: English-Lean hidden-state similarity likely reflects only topic, as similarity alone did far worse than likelihood alone in [formalalign].

compute_axis.quantity: Model size of the model whose hidden states are compared; the test does not vary a parallel-compute quantity

held_fixed: Input normalization: attributes, comments and proofs stripped, theorem name replaced with X, identical formatting for W and F, no chat template
Layer, pooling and normalization chosen by 5-fold CV grouped by PR before any test fold is scored
Cap of 3 pairs per PR, bootstrap clustered by PR
Decision rule fixed before the run

predictions.if_lever: Hidden-state similarity beats the best word-overlap, embedding and likelihood baselines by at least 10 points on fixed-versus-wrong pairs and catches at least 25% of errors the judge missed.
predictions.if_not: Similarity separates matched from random pairs only (topic level), fails to beat cheap baselines on fine pairs, and is redundant with the text judge.
predictions.decision_rule: C1 gate: matched-vs-random AUROC >= 0.90 at best layer for at least one model, else stop. C2 passes if best O4 variant beats best of B1, B2, B3 by >= 10 points two-alternative accuracy (95% cluster-bootstrap CI excluding 0), English-ablated control within 50 +/- 5%, and invariance ratio <= 0.5. C3 passes if O4 flags >= 25% of judge-accepted incorrect items at the judge's false-positive rate and judge+O4 raises AUROC by >= 0.02 with CI excluding 0 on both external sets.
predictions.noise_rule: 95% bootstrap intervals clustered by PR (FC) or problem ID (ProofNetVerif); paired differences use the same bootstrap; Holm correction across the three core models.
predictions.expected_why: FormalAlign found the representation-similarity term alone far worse than the likelihood term, and interp.md doubts fine-grained separation.

plan.compute_tested_why: The test compares scoring methods (activations vs text judge vs baselines) across models and layers; it does not vary a quantity that more parallel compute buys.
plan.scored_against: Human-triaged Formal Conjectures fix pairs (wrong vs fixed Lean), ProofNetVerif and CriticLeanBench labels, and the Qwen3-32B text judge, plus lexical, embedding, likelihood baselines and a supervised probe ceiling.

Qwen3-32B as text judge with CriticLean Template [G] (primary baseline)
Likelihood: certainty and PMI log p(L|E) - log p(L), no fine-tuning
Supervised logistic probe ceiling trained on ProofNetVerif valid (interp.md O3)

baseline.what: Qwen3-32B as a text judge with CriticLean's published prompt, thinking mode, score = fraction of samples judging incorrect

anchor.what: Qwen3-32B as judge on all 500 CriticLeanBench items should reproduce published ACC 85.6, TPR 96.0, TNR 75.2 [criticlean].

checks: Logit reconstruction: final norm plus unembedding on last-layer state matches outputs.logits within bf16 tolerance
Padding and batch invariance: left-padded vector cosine > 0.999 with unbatched
Determinism: two runs give same vectors within tolerance
Tokenizer round-trip decode(encode(x)) == x for every Lean string
Pairing shuffle: C1 retrieval falls to chance (1%)
Positive control: random-pairing negatives must separate
Invariance control: Lean-proven meaning-preserving edits must not move the score
English-ablated control: replace E with random docstring; accuracy above 55% means signal is Lean typicality
Hand-check 50 synthetic meaning-changing edits
Reproduction anchor on CriticLeanBench before trusting judge comparison

Judge baseline B4: Qwen3-32B thinking generations on about 4.1k items plus 3 extra samples on about 1.1k FC W/F items; first reproduce CriticLeanBench anchor

phases.stop_rule: If measured generation rate is lower than needed (about 190 output tokens/s/GPU), cut the extra samples.

records.card: **O4 · Cross-representation comparison of English and Lean.** R4 · interp · random pick · compute tested: no · plan expects: the hypothesis fails · halted: G-plan **Question.** Do a model's hidden states for an English statement and its Lean formalization drift apart when the formalization is wrong, and is that more useful than a text judge or cheap baselines? **What is known.** FormalAlign trained a combined certainty plus similarity scorer; similarity alone scored 45.25/20.75/20.49/21.81 vs certainty 98.98/85.64/53.69/55.55 on Alignment-Selection [formalalign]. Whether untrained or label-free similarity of English and Lean states separates real research-level misformalization fixes, and whether it adds anything to a same-model text judge. **Hypothesis.** Expected to fail on fine-grained errors: English-Lean hidden-state similarity likely reflects only topic, as similarity alone did far worse than likelihood alone in [formalalign]. **If the hypothesis holds.** Hidden-state similarity beats the best word-overlap, embedding and likelihood baselines by at least 10 points on fixed-versus-wrong pairs and catches at least 25% of errors the judge missed. **If not.** Similarity separates matched from random pairs only (topic level), fails to beat cheap baselines on fine pairs, and is redundant with the text judge. **Test.** Compare English and Lean hidden states in Qwen3-32B, Goedel-Prover-V2-32B and Kimina-7B on 715 mined wrong-to-fixed pairs and two benchmarks, against the same model as text judge and cheap baselines [formalalign]. *Compute axis.* Model size of the model whose hidden states are compared; the test does not vary a parallel-compute quantity: 7–32 billion parameters, 2 levels. Closest prior: not on this axis. Prior art checked without web search. *Restructuring.* none. **Check first.** Qwen3-32B as judge on all 500 CriticLeanBench items should reproduce published ACC 85.6, TPR 96.0, TNR 75.2 [criticlean]. Tolerance: +/- 3 points. **Would not show.** Positives are only errors already found, biased toward what judges find. Small named slices (density, Euclidean) are checked item by item only.
